content: 1. Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) immune reconstitution adenitis has been discussed in the context of tuberculosis (TB) management. (Int J Tuberc Lung Dis, 2011). 2. Mathad and Gupta (2012) explored the epidemiology, management, and research gaps in tuberculosis among pregnant and postpartum women, highlighting the unique challenges faced by this population. (Clin Infect Dis, 2012). 3. A Swedish cohort study by Jonsson et al. (2020) demonstrated an increased risk of active tuberculosis during pregnancy and the postpartum period, emphasizing the need for targeted interventions. (Eur Respir J, 2020). 4. Loto and Awowole (2012) reviewed tuberculosis in pregnancy, providing insights into its clinical implications and management strategies. (J Pregnancy, 2012). 5. Gupta et al. (2007) investigated postpartum tuberculosis incidence and mortality among HIV-infected women and their infants in Pune, India, between 2002 and 2005, revealing significant health risks in this demographic. (Clin Infect Dis, 2007). 6. Maternal tuberculosis has been identified as a risk factor for mother-to-child transmission of HIV, as reported by Gupta et al. (2011). (J Infect Dis, 2011). 7. Gomes et al. (Thorax, 2011). 8. Zennér et al. (2012) conducted a national cohort study in the UK, identifying pregnancy as a period of increased tuberculosis risk, which necessitates enhanced screening and care. (Am J Respir Crit Care Med, 2012). 9. Sugarman et al. (2014) estimated the global burden of tuberculosis in pregnancy, highlighting its significant impact on maternal and neonatal health. (Lancet Glob Health, 2014). 10. The SHINE trial protocol (2018) proposed shorter treatment regimens for minimal tuberculosis in children, aiming to improve adherence and outcomes. (Trials, 2018). 11. The integration of palliative care into tuberculosis management has been emphasized as a critical component of comprehensive care, particularly for drug-resistant TB cases. (WHO, 2020). 12. Connor et al. (2012) issued a declaration on palliative care for multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis, advocating for improved support systems. (Int J Tuberc Lung Dis, 2012). 13. The USAID/TB CARE II project developed comprehensive guidelines for palliative care and support in tuberculosis, addressing the needs of patients with drug-resistant TB. (Accessed March 2022). 14. WHO operational handbooks provide detailed guidance on tuberculosis prevention, diagnosis, and treatment, including modules on pediatric TB management and drug-resistant TB care. (WHO, 2022). 15. Tuberculin skin testing (TST) remains a standard method for identifying Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection, with specific protocols for administration, reading, and interpretation outlined in WHO guidelines. (WHO, 2014). 16. Sample collection methods for diagnosing tuberculosis in children include respiratory specimens (e.g., sputum, gastric aspirates) and non-respiratory specimens (e.g., cerebrospinal fluid, serosal fluids). These methods are tailored to the age and clinical condition of the patient. (WHO, 2022). 17. Research has highlighted the importance of integrating tuberculosis care into broader health services, such as malnutrition management and HIV care, to address overlapping health challenges in high-burden settings. (Lancet, 2013; Public Health Action, 2017). 18. Training materials and resources for healthcare workers have been developed to enhance the diagnosis and management of pediatric tuberculosis, with a focus on family-centered approaches and early detection. (WHO, 2021). 19. Advocacy efforts continue to emphasize the need for increased funding and innovation in tuberculosis research, particularly for diagnostics, preventive treatments, and care models tailored to children and adolescents. (Treatment Action Group, 2021). 20. The WHO operational handbook on tuberculosis provides a roadmap for ending TB in children and adolescents, with specific modules addressing prevention, screening, diagnosis, and treatment. (WHO, 2022). This summary reflects the key points and findings from the references provided, focusing on tuberculosis management, research, and care across various populations.
